title.value: The need for privacy with public digital contact tracing during the COVID-19 pandemic
title.justification: The title is mentioned at the beginning of the document and reflects the main topic discussed throughout the paper.
title.quote: The need for privacy with public digital contact tracing during the COVID-19 pandemic

analysis.description: This paper discusses the use of digital contact tracing applications during the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on privacy concerns and the need for a privacy-protecting approach. It emphasizes the use of machine learning to enhance contact tracing while safeguarding individual privacy to maintain public trust.

type.justification: The paper discusses real-world applications and the societal impact of digital contact tracing, including examples from various countries, which indicate an empirical approach.
type.quote: Mobile phone-enabled digital contact tracing colocalises individuals in time and space through the use of GPS, Bluetooth, or other such technologies. Google and Apple have promised to provide frameworks for how to use their technologies for contact tracing.

name.justification: The paper addresses the use of digital technologies in healthcare, specifically in the context of digital contact tracing for COVID-19.
name.quote: Digital technologies are already increasingly used in the context of health-care delivery and clinical trials.

name.justification: The paper extensively discusses the privacy implications of digital contact tracing applications.
name.quote: Despite the potential advantages, most of the applications in use or under consideration have an impact on individual privacy that democratic societies would normally consider to be unacceptably high.

name.justification: The paper mentions the epidemiological impact and control of the COVID-19 pandemic through digital contact tracing.
name.quote: Various behavioral messages can be delivered quickly to enable the individual to take appropriate, measured action. These multiple advantages have the potential to establish rapid epidemiological control of the pandemic.

name.justification: The model is referenced through the mention of a paper by Lecun, Bengio, and Hinton on deep learning strategies to enhance tracing systems.
name.quote: Machine-learning strategies can improve on simple binary contact tracing systems by providing methods to calculate quantifiable individual risk.

is_contributed.justification: The paper does not introduce a new deep learning model but references the concept in the context of contact tracing.
is_contributed.quote: Lecun Y, Bengio Y, Hinton G. Deep learning. Nature 2015; 521: 436–44.

is_executed.justification: There is no indication that the models were executed as part of this study.
is_executed.quote: Pseudonymised data should be used to inform machine-learning models, and only these data should be stored centrally on a protected server.

is_compared.justification: The paper does not compare deep learning models numerically but rather discusses their potential use.
is_compared.quote: Machine-learning strategies can improve on simple binary contact tracing systems by providing methods to calculate quantifiable individual risk.

referenced_paper_title.justification: This is the title of the paper by Lecun, Bengio, and Hinton referenced in the text.
